purpose: Estazolam is used to help you fall asleep and stay asleep when you have trouble sleeping (insomnia). It is meant for short-term use, usually no more than 1 to 2 weeks. Your doctor may prescribe it when other sleep strategies have not worked well enough.
how_it_works: Estazolam works by calming your brain and nervous system. It boosts the effect of a natural chemical in your brain called GABA, which slows down brain activity and helps you feel relaxed and sleepy. Think of it like turning down the volume on an overactive brain so you can drift off to sleep more easily.
common_side_effects: Drowsiness or grogginess the next morning, dizziness, headache, dry mouth, feeling uncoordinated or unsteady, and mild memory problems are the most common side effects. Most of these improve as your body gets used to the medicine.
warnings: This medicine can be habit-forming, so do not take it longer or in higher doses than prescribed. Do not drink alcohol while taking it — this combination can be very dangerous and even life-threatening. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you have a history of addiction, breathing problems, liver disease, or depression. Stopping suddenly can cause withdrawal symptoms, so always talk to your doctor before stopping.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 mg taken by mouth at bedtime. Your doctor may start you on a lower dose of 0.5 mg if you are older or more sensitive to medications. The maximum dose is 2 mg. Always take it right before you plan to sleep and only when you have at least 7 to 8 hours available for rest.
